01_network: FULL ALCE architecture and the CAAA family training objective. Neural comparators share the two-layer bidirectional network; prespecified removal controls disable their designated components. Climate context enters nonlinear joint attention and is also concatenated directly with its weighted hidden mean. The heavy-event head produces logits during training with BCEWithLogitsLoss and probabilities through sigmoid for reporting. The event is observed rainfall strictly greater than each client’s TRAIN q80; the fixed probability cutoff is 0.5. Inputs use shared TRAIN scaling; target scaling and q80 are fitted locally. CAAA climate relevance uses fixed whole-TRAIN severity and two local sensitivity summaries; inner-monitor performance varies by round. The proximal coefficient uses eligible batch-example severity. Outer validation selects hyperparameters and global/personal checkpoints, never gradient updates. The selected primary aggregation coefficients are (1,0,0), so its performance and climate aggregation terms are inactive; the anchor removal experiments use (0.3,0.3,0.4). This is a one-process simulation with plain summaries and no secure aggregation or differential privacy. Graph controls require separate privileged access to aligned TRAIN rainfall; centralized and static-router controls use declared raw pooling.
02_messages: CAAA family communication flow in the recorded one-process simulation. Model states and scalar monitoring/validation diagnostics are transferred each round, together with two fixed whole-TRAIN climate strengths. Counts and two local sensitivity correlations are one-time uploads. Shared input scaling uses plain TRAIN count/sum/squared-sum vectors, with mean and SD broadcast. Target mean/SD and q80 are fitted locally; two float64 target summaries are exported for inverse decoding (16 bytes/client), and q80 is exposed in schema and evaluation diagnostics. These are recorded reporting exports. Full local training rows are not required for CAAA parameter updates. The selected primary coefficients are (1,0,0), making performance and climate aggregation terms inactive; the anchor experiments use (0.3,0.3,0.4). This is no secure-aggregation or differential-privacy implementation, and scalar/summary sharing can reveal information. Graph controls separately use privileged aligned TRAIN rainfall; centralized and static-router controls use declared raw-data pooling. The network and training equation are shown in 01_network.
03_input_availability: Calendar support for a target month t issued at00:00 UTC on its first day. Historical origins span t−12 through t−1. Rainfall features include lags1,2,5,11 relative to each origin and trailing3/6/12-month statistics ending one month before it, giving combined CHIRPS support t−24 through t−2. Climate period ends span t−13 through t−2; the underlying overlapping ONI and MEIv2 periods begin at t−15 and t−14. Meteorological inputs span t−15 through t−4. Known season harmonics do not use observed target rainfall. The prespecified availability sensitivity delays observed inputs by one further month. These support rules avoid using future observations but are archive-availability assumptions, not established real-time product vintages or optimized physical propagation lags.
04_fixed_domains: Frozen study domains intersected with Natural Earth5.1.1 country geometry. Bounding boxes are shown in the source coordinate system; each source mask selects native grid centers within the country and half-open box bounds and weights the whole selected cell area on WGS84. Native grids are not resampled. C1 and C5 overlap, and the five study domains do not partition or fully cover India. This is a study-domain map, not an April–June2025 rainfall map or a forecast.
